title: Utilization of Microscale Silicon Cantilevers to Assess Cellular Contractile Function In Vitro
protocol: Bake Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers at 125 °C for 20 min to dehydrate them.
Deposit a 1.5 µm thick layer of silicon oxide onto the handle layer of the SOI wafer using PECVD.
Dispense 2 ml of P20 primer on the center of the wafer and spin at 3,000 rpm for 60 sec at an acceleration of 1,000 rpm/sec.
Dispense 2 ml of S1818 photoresist on the center of the wafer and spin at 3,000 rpm for 60 sec at an acceleration of 1,000 rpm/sec to obtain a 1.5 µm thick layer of photoresist.
Perform a soft bake at 115 °C for 1 min on a hot plate.
Calculate the exposure time based on an exposure energy value of 125 mJ/cm² for S1818 photoresist.
Immerse the wafer in a 726 MIF photoresist developer for 1 min while gently shaking it back and forth.
Rinse the wafer with de-ionized (DI) water.
Dry the wafer, preferably using a spin rinse dryer (SRD) tool.
Remove photoresist from the wafer edge using a cotton swab dipped in acetone.
Load the wafer into a DRIE tool with the photoresist side facing up.
Etch the patterned silicon layer through the device layer using the DRIE tool.
Place the etched wafer in a hot photoresist bath solution for 20 minutes to strip the photoresist.
Transfer the wafer to a quick-dump-rinser (QDR) and rinse with DI water.
Load the wafer into an SRD tool to rinse and dry the wafer.
Inspect the wafer under a microscope to ensure the cantilever pattern appears as expected.
Deposit a 1 µm thick layer of un-doped silicon oxide on the device layer using a PECVD tool.
Place the wafer on the spin coater chuck with the handle layer facing up.
Center the wafer on the spin coater chuck.
Dispense 2 ml of P20 primer onto the center of the wafer.
Spin the wafer at 3,000 rpm for 60 seconds at an acceleration of 1,000 rpm/sec.
Dispense 2 ml of SPR220-4.5 photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
Spin at 2,000 rpm for 45 seconds at an acceleration of 1,000 rpm/sec to obtain a 6.5 µm thick layer of photoresist.
Place the wafer on a proximity hot plate and perform a soft bake at 115 °C for 2 minutes.
Align the backside window mask to the front side cantilever pattern using a photolithography contact aligner capable of front/back alignment.
Perform a hard contact UV exposure with an exposure time calculated based on an energy value of 480 mJ/cm² for SPR220-4.5 photoresist.
Let the wafers remain in a dark area for 30 minutes before the next processing step.
Immerse the wafer in a 726 MIF photoresist developer and gently shake it back and forth for 2 minutes to develop the photoresist.
Rinse the wafer with de-ionized (DI) water.
Dry the wafer, preferably using a spin rinse dryer (SRD) tool.
Place the wafers in an oven at 90 °C for 12 hours.
Etch the silicon oxide layer on the backside of the wafer using an RIE system with fluorinated gases and a recipe for etching oxide.
Inspect the wafers under a microscope to ensure that the silicon oxide in the exposed window is completely etched.
Remove the photoresist on the edge of the wafer using a clean room swab dipped in acetone.
Load the wafer into a DRIE tool and run a recipe to etch the patterned handle layer to a depth of 500 µm with the buried oxide layer functioning as an etch stop.
Split this etch into multiple runs to prevent excessive heating of the wafer, which causes inconsistent etching of the silicon.
Perform a wet etching step using 25% dilute HF etchant to strip the buried oxide layer below the cantilevers and the protective oxide layer on top of the cantilevers.
Rinse the wafer using a series of DI water baths.
Carefully dry the wafer with nitrogen without applying forceful sprays directly on the cantilevers.
Cleave individual chips from the wafer along the cleave lines produced during the handle layer etch step.
Prepare 13F coverslips according to previously published methods.
Sterilize cantilever chips and 13F coverslips in a 70% ethanol solution.
Allow sterilized items to air dry in a flow hood.
Place individual cantilever chips on top of 13F coverslips inside a standard 12 well plate.
Coat the cantilevers with the biopolymer or surface modification optimized for the cell type according to the standard cell culture protocols.
Resuspend cells in their specific growth medium to the desired concentration, typically at 3-4x more concentrated than for standard coverslip preparations.
Pipette 200 μl of the cell suspension onto the cantilever chip surface, ensuring a bubble of medium covers the cantilever windows entirely.
Replace the 13F coverslip and reattempt the plating if the medium wicks through the window without forming a static bubble on top of the cantilevers.
Transfer the plate containing the chips to an incubator and allow the cells to adhere for at least 1 hr (preferably 2-3 hr).
Use sterile forceps to transfer the chip to a clean well, without a 13F coverslip, after the plating period.
Top up the culture with 1 ml of growth medium.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Maintain cells according to their standard protocol for in vitro maintenance on coverslips.
Switch medium composition to induce myotube formation when skeletal muscle cells become confluent.
Place a heated culture dish into the stage of an upright electrophysiology microscope.
Add 3 ml of feeding medium containing 10 mM HEPES to the heated microscope stage.
Mount stainless steel electrodes inside the heated culture dish at a separation distance of 15 mm.
Connect the electrodes to a pulse generator capable of producing field stimulation pulses.
Bolt a Helium-Neon laser, mounted on XY translational stages, to the underside of the microscope table.
Adjust the laser beam to direct it through the base of the heated culture dish at a 30° angle.
Bolt a quadrant photo-detector module, mounted on XY translational stages, to the underside of the microscope stage.
Adjust the position so that the reflected laser beam lands in the center of the 4 quadrants.
Write a software program to control the linear actuators that scan across the cantilevers.
Turn on the cantilever analysis hardware and associated software.
Insert the heated stage thermistor into the medium and wait for it to read 37 °C.
Insert the cantilever chip into the stage with the cantilevers oriented toward the right hand side of the stage.
Focus the microscope to bring the edges of the cantilevers into view.
Use the laser/photo-detector control software to position the laser beam on the tip of cantilever 1.
Press “play” on the recording software.
Position the photo-detector so that the signal reads “0” in both x and y frames by adjusting the stepper motors controlling the photo-detector.
Set cantilever 1 position in the laser/photo-detector control software.
Move the laser to the tip of cantilever 16.
Repeat step to set the position for cantilever 16 in the laser/photo-detector control software.
Move the laser to the tip of cantilever 32.
Repeat step 4.7.
Set cantilever 32 position in the laser/photo-detector control software.
Move the laser to the tip of cantilever 17.
Repeat step 4.7.
Set cantilever 17 position in the laser/photo-detector control software.
Turn off the microscope light source.
Turn off the overhead light in the laboratory.
Press “record” on the recording software.
Set the pulse generator hardware to 40 msec, 5 V pulses at a frequency of 1 Hz.
Turn the machine on.
Using the laser/photo-detector control software, set the hardware to scan across the 32 cantilever array.
Stop for 5 sec at each one.
Examine the recorded trace from each cantilever for evidence of contractile activity.
Make a note of each cantilever with positive responses.
Remove any non-responsive cantilevers from the scan protocol on the laser/photo-detector control software.
Rescan the active cantilevers without stimulation.
Obtain a reading of the cell’s spontaneous contractile activity.
Run scans with or without broad field electrical stimulation.
Add a therapeutic compound to the medium before scanning.
Carry out fatigue assessments by electrically stimulating cells for extended periods.
Scan levels of contractility to measure time until peak force drops below threshold.
Measure neuromuscular junction formation in co-cultures of motor neurons and muscle.
Treat motoneuron-myotube cantilever co-cultures with a neuronal stimulant.
Scan for increases in spontaneous activity after treatment with stimulants.
Treat cultures with a synaptic inhibitor to decrease spontaneous activity.
Scan for decreases in spontaneous activity after treatment with inhibitors.
Use modified Stoney’s equations to convert raw cantilever deflection data into stress measurements.
Convert raw cantilever deflection data into cellular contractile force measurements.
